identificationModule.briefTitle: Reducing Reconsolidation of Trauma Memories With Propranolol
identificationModule.officialTitle: Reduction of the Reconsolidation of the Trauma Memory With Propranolol

descriptionModule.briefSummary: The purpose of this study is to test whether propranolol is capable of reducing subsequent physiological trauma-related conditioned responses, as well as self-reported post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD) symptoms.

armGroups.label: Propranolol + Memory Reactivation
armGroups.description: This arm involves recalling the traumatic event after administration of propranolol

armGroups.label: Placebo + Memory reactivation
armGroups.description: This arm involves recalling the traumatic event after administration of a placebo

armGroups.label: Placebo + No Memory Reactivation
armGroups.description: This arm involves administration of a placebo without recalling the traumatic event

armGroups.label: Propranolol + No Memory Reactivation
armGroups.description: This arm involves administration of propranolol without recalling the traumatic event

armGroups.label: Open-label Propranolol + Memory Reactivation
armGroups.description: All participants terminating the double-blind phase of the study will receive open-label reconsolidation blockade treatment with propranolol combined with recall of the traumatic event for six weeks.
interventionNames: Drug: Short acting + long acting propranolol + memory reactivation

interventions.name: Short acting + long acting propranolol + memory reactivation
interventions.description: After completing the double-blind phase of the study, participants will receive short acting propranolol 1mg/kg (patient weight) + long acting propranolol (1 or 1.5 mg/kg) followed by memory reactivation. Dose level for the long-acting propranolol will be randomly assigned across participants.

secondaryOutcomes.description: PTSD symptom levels will be assessed 2 to 26 weeks after randomization
Quality of life assessments will be conducted 2 to 26 weeks following randomization
The Memory Experiences Questionnaire will be administered from 2 to 26 weeks following randomization
Psychophysiological assessments will be repeated 26 weeks following randomization
